subject: Request: quality-gated canary (prompt-set gating + auto-rollback) for Orion Finance pilot
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen@orionfinance.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Request: quality-gated canary (prompt-set gating + auto-rollback) for Orion Finance pilot

Team —

Quick background: Orion Finance (cc'd) is moving toward a Q4 pilot with Redwood for our dedicated Private offering. Their legal and risk teams require a stronger safety net on model rollouts — specifically, they want a canary mechanism that gates rollouts against a fixed prompt-set and automatically rolls back if a quality regression threshold is hit. This is a gating requirement in their procurement checklist and is a go/no-go for their pilot kickoff.

Ask: Can Eng/Product prioritize a scoped feature: "quality-gated canary" that includes:
- an immutable prompt-set attachable to a canary rollout (customer-supplied and stored as an artifact)
- per-rollout evaluation against that prompt-set with pass/fail thresholds (configurable, e.g., 95% pass on logits/response metrics)
- automatic rollback policy (auto-revert to previous model/variant when threshold is breached N times in M minutes)
- telemetry exported to Orion's S3/secure endpoint and surfaced in Console as a per-rollout pass/fail indicator

Why this matters: this feature is explicitly requested in the SOW and speeds procurement by avoiding manual evaluation steps. If we don't provide something concrete, Orion will push the pilot to a later wave or ask for contractual credits.

Attachments: orion_requirements_v2.pdf (requirements & procurement note), ORF-MAP-2027.xlsx (mutual action plan)

I realize this is cross-functional (Product + Eng + CS + Sales). Can we get an initial feasibility estimate and a decision on prioritization by EOD Wed so I can update Orion's procurement team?

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen@orionfinance.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: quality-gated canary (prompt-set gating + auto-rollback) for Orion Finance pilot

Thanks for the clear ask, Priyom —

This aligns closely with the rollout/gating work we've been discussing in Product, but there are a few specifics we need to scope before committing to EOD:
1) Prompt-set storage: do we need to support signed customer artifacts (immutable) and retention policies?
2) Evaluation metrics: Orion asked for "quality" thresholds — is that a quantitative metric we can compute (e.g., ROUGE/BLEU/embedding similarity/LLM-eval) or will they supply ground-truth judgments?
3) Auto-rollback safety: what is the allowed blast radius? Do we rollback the single canary shard, the route, or the entire tenant?

Ben / Karthik — can Eng weigh in on estimated complexity? If we build this as a feature flag + evaluation worker + control-plane hook, rough ballpark implementation could be 2-3 sprints with a small team, but that depends on metrics and telemetry integration designs.

Grace
PM, Rollouts & Reliability

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 02:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: quality-gated canary (prompt-set gating + auto-rollback) for Orion Finance pilot

Grace — quick notes from Eng on complexity and constraints:
- Prompt-set storage + immutability: straightforward; we can leverage existing artifact storage and add a signed manifest. Low effort (~3 engineer-weeks).
- Evaluation engine: medium complexity. We have evaluation infra but must add plugin for customer-supplied prompt-sets and batch eval. Expect ~6-8 engineer-weeks to expose safe, configurable thresholds and produce per-rollout metrics.
- Auto-rollback: risky surface. Implementing rollout hooks that can trigger automated revert is doable but requires careful guardrails (rate limits + manual override + telemetry). Estimate ~4-6 engineer-weeks for a minimal safe implementation.
- Telemetry export: we can stream summarized pass/fail events to customer endpoint; full-text exports are high-touch (PII concerns) and will require contracts and security review.

Rough total: 3-4 engineer-months for a minimal MVP (feature-flagged, limited to PRD/Dedicated customers), assuming Product scopes evaluation metrics to the simplest integrable signal (e.g., model-score delta + token-level heuristics).

Ben: for prioritization, what's the business impact / ACV if we deliver this before Orion's pilot start?

Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 14:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: quality-gated canary (prompt-set gating + auto-rollback) for Orion Finance pilot

Short answer on business impact: Orion is a mid-size regional bank; pilot would convert to a paid Dedicated contract at ~USD 480k ARR within 9 months if successful, with an option for a multi-year private deployment. If we can ship a scoped MVP before their pilot kickoff (requested for late July), it materially reduces procurement friction.

That said, we should avoid a big-scoped whiteboard that delays GA. Proposal: Product and Eng scope an MVP with these constraints:
- support only ROUGE-like automated metric + token-similarity for the prompt-set (no human-in-the-loop initially)
- limit rollout scope to a single route/tenant shard with manual escalation if rollback is triggered more than twice in 24h
- telemetry export limited to metadata + pass/fail, no raw responses

If Product signs off on the scope, Sales will commit to a pilot kickoff date and can adjust MAP to include a short beta clause. Priyom: I can commit one solutions-engineer for evaluation support during pilot.

Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales

From: Ellen Park <ellen@orionfinance.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: quality-gated canary (prompt-set gating + auto-rollback) for Orion Finance pilot

Thanks, everyone — appreciate the clear technical outline and proposed MVP constraints. A few clarifications from our side that affect scoping: 
- We will provide the prompt-set and an initial ground-truth sample (50 examples) for calibration; exports should be metadata-only for now.
- Pilot kickoff needs to be the week of 25 July. If Redwood can provide the MVP (as scoped by Ben) and an SOW addendum for the gating behavior, Procurement can sign the pilot SOW this month.

This timeline is tight but feasible if you can prioritize the MVP. Procurement is OK with a short-term beta clause and an additional security review for artifact handling.

Ellen Park
VP, Product & Innovation, Orion Finance
